title: Unambiguous uplink jamming during quiet space weather
description: The positive control. Quiet geomagnetic conditions, a narrow-band interference signature with a stable bearing that resolves to a known emitter site, corroborated independently by an ally and by a commercial operator. Correct end state: hostile probability high, attribution to northern_fleet, and the belief crossing must happen at the signature inject and not before it.

injects.content: Geomagnetic conditions quiet to unsettled, Kp 2. No significant solar activity in the last 72 hours. No storm watches in effect. High-latitude propagation nominal.

Uplink degradation over the Barents and Svalbard footprint. Carrier-to-noise ratio down sharply on affected beams; the effect starts and stops abruptly rather than fading, and is confined to a geographic footprint rather than following the terminator. Spacecraft health nominal on all affected vehicles.

Interference characterised: narrow-band, high duty cycle, stable centre frequency, pulse repetition interval consistent with a known ground-based uplink jamming system. Bearing stable over six hours and consistent with a fixed site on the Kola peninsula. The emission is not consistent with ionospheric scintillation, which is broadband, variable and follows the geomagnetic indices.

Independent Norwegian collection from the Vardo site gives the same bearing and the same signal characteristics, from a site we have associated with the fleet's electronic warfare units in previous years. We assess deliberate emission with high confidence. We have not yet formed a view on why.

Second operator reports the same footprint and the same spectral signature on an unrelated constellation in a different band. Two independent systems, same geographic boundary, same start and stop times.

Statement rejects reports of interference with civilian satellite services as unfounded. Notes that exercises notified in advance are under way in the region, that all activity is within Russian territory and international norms, and asks which specific satellite is alleged to have been affected and on whose published assessment.

Emission ceased. Service restored across the affected footprint within twenty minutes. Total emission duration approximately 26 hours, intermittent, with gaps that align with the site's local pass geometry rather than with any environmental variable.
